description: Randomly thins out the spectrum: analysis channels are gathered into blocks of adjacent channels, and only keep randomly-chosen blocks are retained in each spectral window — the rest are discarded. Operates on PVOC analysis files (.ana).
musical_use: A random sieve for the spectrum. Unlike trace-style thinning (which always keeps the loudest channels), scatter's random choice may or may not retain the audibly prominent data — results flicker unpredictably between recognisable and ghostly. Low keep values leave a sparse, unstable skeleton of the source; a larger blocksize keeps wider contiguous bands for a more band-filtered character. Time-varying keep and/or blocksize envelopes let a sound disintegrate or re-materialise across its length. Note: re-running with identical arguments reproduces the exact same 'random' selection on this build (see known_issues) — to get a different scatter, change keep, blocksize, or the input.

keep.description: Number of randomly-chosen blocks to keep in each spectral window (range: 1 to the analysis channel count, e.g. 513 for a 1024-point analysis). May vary over time via a breakpoint file.

blocksize.description: Frequency span of each block (default: the width of one analysis channel, ~43 Hz for a 1024-point analysis at 44.1 kHz). Rounded internally to a multiple of the channel width. May vary over time via a breakpoint file attached to the flag (-b<file>).

randcnt.description: Randomise the number of blocks actually kept per window between 1 and keep, instead of always keeping exactly keep.

no_norm.description: Turn OFF normalisation of the resulting sound.

examples.description: Keep 8 random single-channel blocks per window.
examples.expected_use: Reduce a rich spectral source to a sparse, flickering subset of itself.

examples.description: Keep 8 random 300 Hz-wide bands per window.
examples.expected_use: A chunkier random thinning — wider contiguous bands survive, closer to unstable bandpass filtering.

known_issues: Deterministic 'randomness' (headline finding): despite being a random process, blur scatter never seeds its RNG — identical arguments produce bit-identical output on every run. Verified empirically on the Linux source build (runs > 2 s apart, with and without -r: .ana data chunks and resynthesised audio identical; only the header date stamp differs) and confirmed in source (scat_preprocess() lacks the initrand48() call that blur drunk has, and CDP's drand48 shim wraps unseeded rand()). No seed flag exists in banner or manual, so a different scatter requires changing keep/blocksize or the input.

The Phase 2 design doc flagged this mode as a stochastic/phase-sensitive candidate; empirically it is not stochastic run-to-run on this build. If a future CDP build seeds the RNG, phase_sensitive and the determinism notes here must be re-verified.
